$comment: YCGrid MCP tool definitions (single source). Loaded by the yc.mcp server and the yc command line tool; references/mcp-tools.md is generated by gen_tools_doc.py. Only edit this file when changing tools.

server.name: YCGrid
server.title: YCGrid
server.instructions: YCGrid is a spreadsheet that closely mimics Excel; Python code runs in a separate host process and the API uses Excel's names. Start by calling yc_connect and yc_get_workbook_info; the project entry point is main.py. Confirm APIs with yc_api_lookup before writing code. YCGrid reloads automatically when a .py file is saved; call yc_reload_python to wait for it and get an error summary, then test with yc_run_macro, yc_trigger_control and yc_ui_input, and read output and errors with yc_read_console. Tools that run user code may trigger real trades; without the user's consent never use them on macros, buttons or combo boxes related to placing orders.

tools.name: yc_connect
tools.title: Connect to YCGrid
tools.description: Lists the YCGrid instances running on this machine and selects the one the other yc_* tools work on. Without target: selects automatically when the current workspace (program folder) has a matching instance or there is only one instance; otherwise returns the candidates, so call again with target. Other tools apply the same rule automatically when not connected yet. Returns: the instance list (instance_id, pid, program folder, workbook, Python host state, protocol version) and the selected instance.

target.description: Instance to select: instance_id, pid or program folder path.

tools.name: yc_get_workbook_info
tools.title: Workbook overview
tools.description: Gets the overall state of the current workbook; usually the first tool to call. Includes: the file path and whether there are unsaved changes; for every sheet its name, CodeName, index, visibility, used range, number of controls and charts, and whether its Python sheet module file (e.g. sheets/Sheet1.py) exists; defined names; the active sheet and selection; the calculation mode and the last recalculation statistics; Design Mode; a summary of the Python host state. Use include to get only the parts you need and save space.

include.description: Parts to return; all parts when omitted.

tools.name: yc_read_range
tools.title: Read range contents
tools.description: Reads the values, formulas, displayed text or number formats of a range as a table with row numbers and column names. Values: numbers as is, text quoted, blanks empty, errors such as #N/A, dates according to date_mode. Ranges larger than max_cells are truncated with a hint about the row_offset of the next page; use summary_only to just learn the shape of the data. For styles, dependencies and other details use yc_inspect_cells.

address.description: A1 address, may include a sheet prefix or be a defined name, e.g. "B2:K100", "Quotes!A1", "'My Sheet'!A1:C3", "QuoteArea".

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

fields.description: What to read; several may be chosen. Only values by default.

max_cells.description: Maximum number of cells to return.

row_offset.description: Paging: the row within the range to start from (0-based).

date_mode.description: How dates are shown: iso = 2026-10-11T09:00:00; serial = Excel serial number.

summary_only.description: Only return the shape (rows, columns), the first row and each column's kind (number, text or empty).

output.description: Output format: table = readable table; json = 2D array.

tools.name: yc_inspect_cells
tools.title: Inspect cell details
tools.description: Gets the full details of a few cells, for debugging: value and type, formula (both A1 and R1C1), displayed text, effective style (font, fill, borders, alignment, number format), the merged area, data validation and the conditional formatting rules that match. Notes, hyperlinks, market data topic bindings and the dependency tree (precedents and dependents) are not available yet. At most 100 cells at a time; use yc_read_range to read many values.

address.description: A1 address, may include a sheet prefix or be a defined name, e.g. "B2:K100", "Quotes!A1", "'My Sheet'!A1:C3", "QuoteArea".

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

include.description: Details to return. When omitted: value, formula, style, merge. comment, hyperlink, binding, precedents and dependents are not available yet.

dependency_depth.description: How many levels of precedents / dependents to follow (0 = none). Not applied yet: precedents and dependents are not available yet.

max_cells.description: Maximum number of cells to inspect.

tools.name: yc_find
tools.title: Find cells
tools.description: Finds cells by content with the semantics of Excel's Find (supports the * and ? wildcards), or with a regular expression. Searches values or formulas (notes: not available yet), on one sheet or in the whole workbook. Returns the matching addresses and a summary of their contents; beyond max_results the list is truncated and the total is reported.

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

look_in.description: What to search in; comments (notes) is not available yet.

look_at.description: part = partial match; whole = the cell contents must match entirely.

regex.description: Treat what as a regular expression.

tools.name: yc_write_range
tools.title: Write values or formulas
tools.description: Writes values or formulas into a range, like Range.Value / Range.Formula. Pass a 2D array in values (outer = rows, inner = columns, its size must match address), or fill the whole range with one value via fill_value; use one of the two. With mode=auto, strings starting with "=" are formulas; relative references in formulas are adjusted by Excel's rules ("=B2*C2" written to D2:D100 adjusts row by row). It fires Worksheet_Change like a user edit. Like every Python write it is not recorded in the user's undo list and doesn't clear it (ADR 0013): the user can't take it back with Ctrl+Z, and the user's own earlier steps stay. Returns the number of cells written and the shown text of the first rows.

address.description: A1 address, may include a sheet prefix or be a defined name, e.g. "B2:K100", "Quotes!A1", "'My Sheet'!A1:C3", "QuoteArea".

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

values.description: 2D array, outer = rows, inner = columns; every cell may be a string, number, boolean or null (clears the cell).

fill_value.description: A single value that fills the whole range (use either this or values).

mode.description: auto = strings starting with = are formulas; values = always values (text starting with = included); formulas = always formulas.

fire_events.description: Whether to fire events such as Worksheet_Change. Not applied yet: false is only noted in the result; to fire no events, set Application.EnableEvents = False in the host (yc_exec_python target=host).

undoable.description: Not applied: Python's writes are never steps of the user's undo list (ADR 0013).

wait_recalc.description: Wait for the recalculation to finish before returning.

tools.name: yc_format_range
tools.title: Format cells
tools.description: Applies formatting to a range; one call can set several things at once: number format, font, fill, borders, alignment, merging, column width and row height, autofit, clearing. Colors are always "#RRGGBB". borders is an array; each item gives edges (e.g. outline = outside borders, inside = inner gridlines, all = everything), a line style and a color, applied in order. It is not an undo step the user can take back: Python's writes are not recorded in the user's undo list (ADR 0013). Formatting changes don't fire Worksheet_Change (like Excel), but clear=contents or all does. Set conditional formatting and data validation through the object model with yc_exec_python (FormatConditions.Add, Validation.Add).

address.description: A1 address, may include a sheet prefix or be a defined name, e.g. "B2:K100", "Quotes!A1", "'My Sheet'!A1:C3", "QuoteArea".

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

number_format.description: Excel number format code, e.g. "#,##0.00", "0.00%", "yyyy/mm/dd", "[$-404]e/m/d" (ROC calendar year).

font.description: Font settings; only the given fields are set.

style.description: Line style; none removes the border.

merge.description: merge_center = Merge & Center; merge_across = Merge Across (merge row by row); merge = Merge Cells; unmerge = Unmerge Cells.

autofit.description: AutoFit the column width or row height.

clear.description: Clear: formats = formats; contents = contents; all = everything; comments = notes and hyperlinks = hyperlinks are not available yet.

tools.name: yc_edit_structure
tools.title: Edit rows, columns and panes
tools.description: Edits the structure of rows, columns and panes: insert or delete rows, columns and cells (formula references are adjusted by Excel's rules), hide or unhide rows and columns, freeze or unfreeze panes, group or ungroup rows and columns. target uses Excel notation: rows "5:7", columns "C:D", a cell range "B2:C3"; for freezing panes give the first scrollable cell (e.g. "B2" freezes row 1 and column A). Inserting and deleting fire Worksheet_Change. It is not an undo step the user can take back, and inserting or deleting rows or columns clears the user's undo list (ADR 0013).

target.description: Target of the operation, e.g. "5:7", "C:D", "B2:C3"; not needed for unfreeze_panes.

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

shift.description: Shift direction when inserting or deleting cells.

tools.name: yc_manage_sheets
tools.title: Manage sheets
tools.description: Manages sheets: add, delete, rename, move, copy, hide, very hide, unhide, activate, or set the tab color. A sheet's Python module is named after its CodeName (CodeName=Sheet1 -> sheets/Sheet1.py); the CodeName is given when the sheet is added and doesn't change, as in Excel's object model. Deleting a sheet can't be undone and needs confirm=true. Adding a sheet fires Workbook_NewSheet.

sheet.description: Target sheet (name, CodeName or 1-based index); omitted for add.

new_name.description: New name (used by add, rename, copy).

before.description: Place before this sheet (used by add, move, copy).

after.description: Place after this sheet (used by add, move, copy).

tools.name: yc_list_controls
tools.title: List controls
tools.description: Lists the controls on sheets (buttons, combo boxes): name, type, sheet and CodeName, position and size (points), Placement, caption or current value (Value, ListIndex and list source of combo boxes), and whether the matching event functions (e.g. CommandButton1_Click, ComboBox1_Change in sheets/Sheet1.py) exist. Filter with sheet; all sheets when omitted.

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or index; the controls of every sheet when omitted.

check_handlers.description: Check whether the matching Click functions exist.

kind.description: Only list one kind of control.

tools.name: yc_add_control
tools.title: Add a control
tools.description: Adds an ActiveX-style control (button, combo box, check box, option button, toggle button, text box, label, list box, spin button, scroll bar or image) to a sheet, like drawing one in Design Mode on the Developer tab; controls can float anywhere. Position it with cover_range so it exactly covers a cell range (the most common way), or with left, top, width, height (in points). With placement=float_window it is fixed to the window and doesn't scroll. Events go in the sheet's module (sheets/<CodeName>.py): <Name>_Change for combo boxes, text boxes, spin buttons and scroll bars, <Name>_Click for the others (buttons, labels, images, check boxes, option and toggle buttons, list boxes); spin buttons also fire SpinUp / SpinDown, scroll bars Scroll. This tool never edits .py files; it only returns the control name, its actual position and suggested event function templates. It is not an undo step the user can take back: Python's writes are not recorded in the user's undo list (ADR 0013).

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

name.description: Control name; must be a valid Python identifier (Unicode letters allowed); named automatically when omitted (CommandButton1, ComboBox1...).

caption.description: Text on the control (button, check box, option and toggle buttons, label).

cover_range.description: Cell range the control should exactly cover, e.g. "B2:C3" (use either this or left/top/width/height).

placement.description: How it moves with cells: move_and_size = position and size follow the cells (default); move = only moves; free_floating = scrolls with the sheet but doesn't follow the cells; float_window = [YC] fixed to the window, doesn't move when scrolling.

color.description: Not available yet: the control's text color isn't set.

kind.description: Control type: button (CommandButton), combobox, checkbox, optionbutton, togglebutton, textbox, label, listbox, spinbutton, scrollbar or image.

list_fill_range.description: (combobox, listbox) Range of the list source, e.g. "Settings!A2:A20"; read straight from the cells, not through Python. Use either this or items.

linked_cell.description: Two-way bound cell, e.g. "Settings!C1": the value (TRUE / FALSE for check boxes and option buttons, the number for spin buttons and scroll bars, the text otherwise) is written to the cell, and changes of the cell update the control.

style.description: (combobox) dropdown_combo = editable; dropdown_list = select from the list only.

value.description: Initial value: "True" / "False" (checkbox, optionbutton, togglebutton), a number (spinbutton, scrollbar) or text.

group_name.description: (optionbutton) Option buttons with the same group name allow one choice.

tools.name: yc_modify_control
tools.title: Modify or delete a control
tools.description: Modifies the properties, position, size, Placement, list source or current value of a control (button, combo box), or deletes it. When renaming, the result reminds you that the event function names must change too. It is not an undo step the user can take back: Python's writes are not recorded in the user's undo list (ADR 0013).

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

name.description: Name of the control to modify.

new_name.description: New name; must be a valid Python identifier.

cover_range.description: Move and resize it to exactly cover this cell range.

placement.description: How it moves with cells: move_and_size = position and size follow the cells (default); move = only moves; free_floating = scrolls with the sheet but doesn't follow the cells; float_window = [YC] fixed to the window, doesn't move when scrolling.

color.description: Not available yet: the control's text color isn't set.

list_fill_range.description: (combobox) Range of the list source, e.g. "Settings!A2:A20"; read straight from the cells, not through Python. Use either this or items.

linked_cell.description: (combobox) Two-way bound cell, e.g. "Settings!C1": the selection is written to the cell, and changes of the cell update the selection.

style.description: (combobox) dropdown_combo = editable; dropdown_list = select from the list only; unchanged when omitted.

value.description: (combobox) Set the currently selected value (written to linked_cell, but _Change is not fired; use yc_trigger_control to fire it).

tools.name: yc_trigger_control
tools.title: Trigger a control event
tools.description: Simulates a user operating a control: a button Click, or selecting a value in a combo box (fires _Change and writes linked_cell; per-cell OnChange and Worksheet_Change of the cell fire in order too). Runs the user's Python code; never use it without the user's consent when connected to a live trading environment. Returns whether the event ran, how long it took and a summary of the console output.

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

dialogs.description: What to do with a MsgBox / InputBox shown meanwhile: auto = answer with the default button or value automatically and log the prompt; show = show it to the user and wait (limited by timeout_ms).

timeout_ms.description: Maximum wait for completion (milliseconds). On timeout the result known so far is returned, noting that it is still running.

value.description: (event=change) The value to select; list_index works too.

list_index.description: (event=change) Index of the item to select (0-based, like Excel's ListIndex).

tools.name: yc_list_charts
tools.title: List charts
tools.description: Lists the charts on sheets: name, type (XlChartType name), position and size, series (name, source: the =SERIES() formula of a cell range or python for a Python array, number of points of a Python array, primary or secondary axis), the y axis range (null when automatic), whether it is in interactive mode, whether it was pulled out into a chart window.

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the charts of every sheet when omitted.

tools.name: yc_add_chart
tools.title: Add a chart
tools.description: Adds a chart to a sheet (an Excel-style chart drawn with ImPlot), like Shapes.AddChart2 plus SetSourceData. chart_type uses Excel's XlChartType names (xlLine, xlColumnClustered, xlXYScatter, xlArea, xlPie, xlStockOHLC, xlRadar, xlWaterfall, xlHistogram, xlPareto, xlBoxwhisker, xlTreemap, xlSunburst, xlFunnel...). The data source is source (a cell range); set series from Python arrays afterwards with yc_modify_chart or the object model (Topic streams: not available yet). Position it with cover_range or left/top/width/height (points). It is not an undo step the user can take back: Python's writes are not recorded in the user's undo list (ADR 0013).

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

name.description: Chart name; named automatically when omitted (Chart 1...).

plot_by.description: Series by columns or by rows.

cover_range.description: Cell range the chart should exactly cover.

interactive.description: [YC] Allow pan, zoom and box selection (common for market charts).

tools.name: yc_modify_chart
tools.title: Modify or delete a chart
tools.description: Modifies a chart's type, title, legend, axis ranges, series (set or delete, change the source or the Python data, move to the secondary axis, color; binding a Topic stream is not available yet), interactive mode, position and size; pulls it out into a chart window or puts it back on the sheet; or deletes the chart. It is not an undo step the user can take back: Python's writes are not recorded in the user's undo list (ADR 0013).

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

set.description: Properties to change (keys are case-insensitive): chart_type (or type; an XlChartType name), title, has_title, has_legend (or legend), interactive, left, top, width, height, name, x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max, x_auto, y_auto, source (a range). Other keys are refused.

series.description: List of series operations: {op?: set (default) | delete, index? (1-based; omitted = a new series), name?, values? (range), x_values? (range), y? or data? (a Python array), x?, append? (add the y / x points to the series), axis?: primary|secondary, color? (#RRGGBB)}. topic (a Topic stream) is not available yet.

float.description: true: pull out into a chart window; false: put back on the sheet.

tools.name: yc_manage_panels
tools.title: Manage custom panels
tools.description: [YC] Lists, creates, modifies, rebuilds or deletes custom panels (Application.Panels). Panels consist of controls (Label, Button, TextBox, ComboBox, CheckBox, ListBox, Option (option buttons), Spin, Slider, Chart, Separator; Group is accepted but not drawn yet); linked_cell binds a cell both ways and on_action names a macro ("Module1.Foo"). Panels and the values of their controls are saved in the workbook. Panels should normally be built in code in Workbook_Open of main.py; this tool is for inspection and quick experiments.

controls.description: (add / modify) List of controls: {type, name, caption?, linked_cell?, on_action?, list_fill_range?, items?, chart?}.

keep_values.description: (rebuild) Controls with the same name keep their old values.

tools.name: yc_manage_layout
tools.title: Manage windows and layout
tools.description: [YC] Floating sheet windows, containers and layouts: list the current layout (main window, floating windows, containers, docking tree), pull a sheet out into a floating window or put it back in the main window, create / delete containers, dock windows into containers, save or restore named layouts (stored in the workbook).

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

item.description: (dock_into) The item to dock: a sheet name, or kind:name for another item (e.g. "panel:Orders", "chart:Chart 1").

tools.name: yc_scroll_view
tools.title: Scroll and select
tools.description: Sets or reads the view state of a sheet window: scroll to a row/column (ScrollRow, ScrollColumn), the selection, the active cell, zoom, frozen panes. After setting it waits until the screen applies it (the next frame) before returning, which suits calling it before yc_screenshot.

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

goto.description: Like Application.Goto: scroll and select, e.g. "Quotes!B1000".

freeze.description: Upper-left cell of the frozen panes, e.g. "B2"; "none" unfreezes.

tools.name: yc_execute_command
tools.title: Run a UI command
tools.description: Runs the command behind a ribbon button, context menu item or shortcut (like Application.CommandBars.ExecuteMso); command ids such as Bold, MergeCenter, PasteSpecial, FreezePanes. Can also query a command's enabled / pressed state. The command list is in references/ui-coverage.md. May fire events or user code.

query.description: true: only query enabled, pressed and label, don't run it.

tools.name: yc_python_status
tools.title: State of the Python host and data feed processes
tools.description: Shows the state and registrations of the Python host: connection mode (managed, not connected, or disabled by the Trust Center: host.code_disabled is true when the workbook's untrusted code was kept from running and a person must click Enable Content), the interpreter path and version, loaded modules and load errors (with file and line), the macro list, UDFs (name, parameters, vectorize, volatile, async), event handlers, button Click mappings (including buttons whose Click function is missing) and recent exceptions. Stream providers and the data feed processes ([[python.feeds]] in ycgrid.toml) are not available yet. Use it after changing and reloading code to confirm everything is registered correctly.

include.description: Parts to return; host, modules, macros, udfs, events, controls and errors when omitted (streams and feeds: not available yet).

annotations.title: State of the Python host and data feed processes

tools.name: yc_reload_python
tools.title: Reload Python
tools.description: Applies changed Python code and returns a result summary. By default YCGrid reloads automatically after a .py file is saved; if an automatic reload is scheduled or running, this tool waits for it and returns its result instead of loading twice, so calling it after editing confirms how loading went. Flow: first compile-check every module in the program folder; on a syntax error nothing is reloaded (the old code keeps running) and the error location is returned; when it passes, managed mode restarts the host process and attached (debugging) mode re-imports the modules; then it waits for Workbook_Open to finish and returns the new registration summary and the errors meanwhile. While a macro or event is running it waits for it to finish by default. Data feed processes only restart when files they use changed. Note: reloading runs user code such as Workbook_HostShutdown and Workbook_Open.

mode.description: Not applied yet: the current mode decides (auto). restart = restart the host process; soft = only re-import the modules.

restart_feeds.description: Not applied yet: would force a restart of every data feed process ([[python.feeds]] in ycgrid.toml), even when the files they use didn't change.

force.description: Reload even when the compile check finds syntax errors (by default nothing is reloaded then and the errors are returned).

timeout_ms.description: Maximum wait for completion (milliseconds). On timeout the result known so far is returned, noting that it is still running.

tools.name: yc_run_macro
tools.title: Run a macro
tools.description: Runs a macro, or any public function of a module, in the Python host (like Application.Run), with optional arguments. Returns: the return value, the console output meanwhile (print, Debug.Print), exception tracebacks, the duration and a summary of the changed cells. MsgBox / InputBox are answered automatically or shown to the user according to the dialogs parameter. Note: runs user code; get the user's consent first for macros that may send orders or change positions.

name.description: Macro name, e.g. "Module1.RefreshQuotes"; the module name may be omitted when no other module has a function with the same name.

dialogs.description: What to do with a MsgBox / InputBox shown meanwhile: auto = answer with the default button or value automatically and log the prompt; show = show it to the user and wait (limited by timeout_ms).

timeout_ms.description: Maximum wait for completion (milliseconds). On timeout the result known so far is returned, noting that it is still running.

tools.name: yc_exec_python
tools.title: Run a Python snippet
tools.description: Runs a Python snippet like Excel's Immediate window. from yc.excel import * has already run, so Application, Range, Cells, ActiveSheet, Worksheets, WorksheetFunction and the xl / vb constants can be used directly. With target=controller (default) it runs in the MCP tool's own connection: it can read and write the workbook but can't see module variables inside the host. With target=host it runs inside the Python host process and can access user modules (needs [mcp].allow_host_exec=true in ycgrid.toml). Returns stdout, the value of the last expression (repr, truncated when long) and exception tracebacks. Suits detailed queries and operations without a dedicated tool, such as conditional formatting and data validation.

code.description: Python code to run; when the last line is an expression its value is returned.

dialogs.description: What to do with a MsgBox / InputBox shown meanwhile: auto = answer with the default button or value automatically and log the prompt; show = show it to the user and wait (limited by timeout_ms).

timeout_ms.description: Maximum wait for completion (milliseconds). On timeout the result known so far is returned, noting that it is still running.

tools.name: yc_evaluate_formula
tools.title: Evaluate a formula
tools.description: Evaluates an Excel formula directly without writing any cell (like Application.Evaluate), to test formula syntax, function results and UDFs. as_cell is not available yet: formulas are evaluated relative to A1. Returns the value and type, or the error value; array results larger than max_cells are truncated.

formula.description: The formula to evaluate, with or without the leading =.

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

as_cell.description: Not available yet: formulas are evaluated relative to A1.

max_cells.description: Maximum number of cells returned for array results.

tools.name: yc_read_console
tools.title: Read the console
tools.description: Reads YCGrid's Immediate window console: print and Debug.Print output, stderr, exception tracebacks (with file and line), the run log of events and macros, and system messages (connection, reload, overload warnings). The result includes next_cursor; pass it as since_cursor next time to get only new lines.

since_cursor.description: next_cursor from the last call; starts from the most recent lines when omitted.

min_level.description: Minimum level: error = errors only; the other levels return every line.

sources.description: Only these sources; all when omitted. python and system select lines; events, calc and feed are not available yet.

tools.name: yc_python_env
tools.title: Python runtime
tools.description: Queries or manages the project's own portable Python (runtime\python): version, installed packages, differences between requirements.txt and requirements.lock, missing packages (with the import scan results). upgrade and rollback are not available yet: the version is fixed at 3.12. Never touches any other Python on the machine.

version.description: (upgrade) Target version, e.g. "3.13"; upgrade is not available yet.

tools.name: yc_install_packages
tools.title: Install Python packages
tools.description: Installs packages into the project's own runtime\python (installed by uv, the system Python is not touched); on success they are added to requirements.txt, requirements.lock is updated and the host reloads. Without packages it installs every missing package that was detected. offline installs only from runtime\wheels.

tools.name: yc_ui_input
tools.title: Simulate UI input
tools.description: Simulates a user's operations on the UI in order. It goes through the real UI path, so the matching events fire, such as SelectionChange, Change, BeforeDoubleClick, BeforeRightClick and OnKey shortcuts. The type of each step in actions: select (select address); type (type text into the active cell, commit decides whether to press Enter, Tab or stay in edit mode); keys (a key combination such as "Ctrl+C", "F9", "Alt+Down", "Ctrl+Z"); click / double_click / right_click (on the cell at address); scroll_to (scroll address into view); design_mode (switch Design Mode according to on); wait (wait ms milliseconds). Returns whether the input finished, the view afterwards (visible range, selection, active cell) and the last console lines.

address.description: Target address of select, click, double_click, right_click and scroll_to.

text.description: Text for type; starting with = makes it a formula.

commit.description: After type: enter = press Enter; tab = press Tab; none = stay in edit mode.

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

dialogs.description: What to do with a MsgBox / InputBox shown meanwhile: auto = answer with the default button or value automatically and log the prompt; show = show it to the user and wait (limited by timeout_ms).

timeout_ms.description: Maximum wait for completion (milliseconds). On timeout the result known so far is returned, noting that it is still running.

tools.name: yc_screenshot
tools.title: Take a screenshot
tools.description: Captures YCGrid as a PNG image to check formatting, layout, conditional formatting, controls and charts visually. target=range scrolls address into view first and crops only that range (optionally with column names and row numbers); grid = the visible part of the grid; window = the whole window (ribbon and status bar included). Returns the image and a description of the visible range. Charts and controls on the sheet are included; floating windows are not in the main window's screenshot.

address.description: The range to capture with target=range.

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

include_headers.description: Whether to include column names and row numbers.

max_width.description: Maximum image width (pixels); larger images are scaled down proportionally.

tools.name: yc_calculate
tools.title: Recalculate and calculation statistics
tools.description: Triggers a recalculation and reports statistics: the number of dirty cells, dependency depth, duration, threads used, locations of circular references, the number of volatile formulas, the actual publish intervals and overload count of recent cycles, and the time spent waiting for Python UDFs. scope=stats_only only reads the statistics without recalculating.

scope.description: dirty = only what changed (F9); full = everything (Ctrl+Alt+F9); stats_only = only read statistics. sheet (the active sheet only) is not available yet and recalculates like dirty; rebuild recalculates like full.

sheet.description: Not applied yet.

tools.name: yc_topics
tools.title: Market data topics
tools.description: Tests the real-time market data channel. push: push test values that simulate market data to test formulas, conditional formatting and the Worksheet_LiveChange event (testing only; real market data is pushed by data feed processes); lookup: the formulas of the cells at address (topic bindings are formulas such as =QUOTE("2330","Bid")). list (the topics) and stats (throughput and latency) are not available yet.

values.description: Values for push, matching topics one to one.

tools.name: yc_ui_state
tools.title: UI state
tools.description: Everything YCGrid shows, in one call and without a screenshot: whether the window is visible, the file, the open dialog (0 = none), the status bar text, operator mode, safety alarms, every sheet (name, used range, tables, charts), the active sheet, cell, selection and the active cell's value and formula, the bound tables (rows, recorded or not), the open yc.plot figures with their plots and items, the replay state and whether the Python host is ready. Use it to check the result of an action before taking a screenshot.

tools.name: yc_bound_tables
tools.title: Bound tables
tools.description: The live tables fed by key through shared memory (ws.bind / yc.data). list: each table's name, sheet, key column, declared columns and formats, freshness limit, whether it is recorded, and age (seconds since its newest row update; null before any data). read: a table's rows by column (numbers, text, dates as ISO text), read columnar through shared memory, up to max_rows.

table.description: The table to read (any table, not only bound ones).

max_rows.description: At most this many rows for read.

tools.name: yc_replay
tools.title: Record and replay
tools.description: Records the data reaching the bound tables to a .yctape file and replays it into the same tables (yc.replay; Trading > Record / Replay). While a replay runs, live data for its tables are ignored, so the screen and its Python code run on recorded data unchanged; live goes back to live data and restores the tables. Actions: status, record (path optional: the workbook's recordings folder; tables optional: the tables marked for recording), stop_recording, play (path, speed: 0 = as fast as possible, start seconds, loop), pause, resume, seek (seconds), speed, live. Returns the replay status: mode (live / replay / paused / ended), position, length, speed, frames, the recording.

path.description: The .yctape file for record and play.

speed.description: Replay speed (play, speed); 0 = as fast as possible.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the recording (play).

loop.description: Replay again from the start at the end (play).

tools.name: yc_workbook_file
tools.title: Workbook file
tools.description: Workbook file operations: save, save as (a single .ycg file, a copy as .xlsx, or the active sheet's values as .csv, which leaves the workbook's own file as it was), open (.ycg, .xlsx / .xlsm, .csv: Excel and CSV files open as a new, untitled workbook), new, export_pdf (a sheet or every visible sheet printed with its page setup). Saving is atomic, so a failure halfway never damages the original. Open and new replace the current workbook; with unsaved changes they only run with discard_changes=true. Fires Workbook_BeforeSave (a handler setting Cancel.Value = True stops the save) and Workbook_AfterSave for save / save_as, Workbook_BeforeClose and the new project's Workbook_Open for open / new.

path.description: File path (used by save_as, open and export_pdf).

sheet.description: export_pdf: the sheet to export (default: the active sheet).

all_sheets.description: export_pdf: export every visible sheet into one PDF.

format.description: Save As format; decided by the extension when omitted.

discard_changes.description: Discard the current unsaved changes when opening or creating a workbook.

tools.name: yc_app_options
tools.title: Application options
tools.description: Reads or sets options of the running application. Without set it returns the current values. Settable: calculation (automatic / manual), enable_events, design_mode, status_bar (status bar text; null restores it), zoom (10-400), display_gridlines, display_formulas. publish_interval_ms, calc_policy and screen_updating are not available yet.

publish_interval_ms.description: Not available yet: the data refresh interval (milliseconds).

calc_policy.description: Not available yet: the calculation policy.

screen_updating.description: Not available yet: whether the screen updates (Application.ScreenUpdating).

status_bar.description: Status bar text; null restores the default.

set.description: Options to change; only the given fields are set.

tools.name: yc_workbook_store
tools.title: Workbook KV store
tools.description: Reads and writes the workbook's built-in key / value store (ThisWorkbook.Store, and Excel-compatible CustomDocumentProperties), e.g. the UI version number ui.version. Values are data JSON can represent; writing marks the workbook as unsaved.

sheet.description: Sheet name, CodeName or 1-based index; the active sheet when omitted. Ignored when address already has a sheet prefix.

tools.name: yc_api_lookup
tools.title: Look up the Python API
tools.description: Looks up the documentation of the YCGrid Python object model (Excel compatible); YCGrid doesn't need to be running. Look up classes, members, constants, events, functions or Excel idioms, e.g. "Range.End", "Borders", "xlUp", "Worksheet_Change", "VLookup", "CommandButton", "UndoGroup". Returns the signature, parameters, description, the matching Excel idiom, whether it is a YCGrid extension [YC], the implementation status and examples. Use it to confirm a member really exists before writing code; don't invent APIs.

query.description: Query string, such as a class name, Class.Member, a constant name, an event name or an Excel snippet.

tools.name: yc_extract_macros
tools.title: Extract Excel macro code
tools.description: Extracts the macro project from an existing Excel file (.xlsm, .xlsb, .xls, .xlam): the code of standard modules, class modules, sheet modules (with CodeName), ThisWorkbook (maps to main.py) and UserForms, plus the controls on sheets: buttons (name, caption, position and OnAction macro of form and ActiveX buttons) and ActiveX combo boxes (name, position, ListFillRange, LinkedCell, Style) are listed in full so they can be rebuilt with yc_add_control; other controls only get name and type, to decide how to replace them. From an .xls file only the macro code is extracted, not the controls (save it as .xlsm in Excel to list them). This is the first step of porting old macros to YCGrid Python. YCGrid doesn't need to be running and no macro is ever executed. Only the macro code and the control list are read, not cell data; ask the user to copy the sheet contents in Excel and paste them into YCGrid.

include_controls.description: Also list the controls on sheets.

modules.description: Only these modules; all when omitted.

max_chars_per_module.description: Maximum characters returned per module; longer modules are truncated with a note.

tools.name: yc_plot_input
tools.title: Operate a plot figure
tools.description: Does what the mouse would do on a yc.plot figure, in data coordinates, through the same events: the figure's Python callbacks (fig.on, handles' on_move / on_release, context menu items) run as for the real mouse. Use it to test chart interactions. Actions run in order; figures are found by id or key (yc_ui_state lists them with their handles and menu items).

figure.description: The figure's key, or its id.

actions.description: The steps, in order. Times as Unix seconds.

action.description: What the mouse does; wheel: zoom (a following plot stops following), live: click the Paused badge (follow again).

x.description: click / double_click / drag_handle / context_menu: the x in data coordinates.

y.description: click / double_click / drag_handle / drag_band_edge / context_menu: the y in data coordinates.

button.description: click: the mouse button; right opens the figure's context menu at x, y (as the mouse would; choose an item with context_menu).

handle.description: drag_handle / drag_band_edge / close_handle: the handle's id or label (yc_ui_state lists them; close_handle clicks a closable line's x button, e.g. cancelling an order drawn by Axes.orders).

plot.description: This step's plot, when not the tool's.

tools.name: yc_panel_input
tools.title: Operate a panel control
tools.description: Clicks a button of a custom panel (Application.Panels) or sets a control's value like the user, so its OnAction / Change runs in the Python host and its LinkedCell is written. Runs the user's Python code; never use it without the user's consent when connected to a live trading environment.

value.description: set_value: the new value (text, number or true / false).
